references.text: In the following verses, the disciples discuss whether the sin is due to the father or the son, which relates directly to the question of the cause of suffering in the case of the man born blind.
The blind man's testimony that it has never been heard that anyone has opened the eyes of someone born blind underscores the unique nature of the miracle and confirms Jesus' divine authority.
Jesus explains that he came to judge, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind, interpreting the physical healing as a picture of the spiritual situation.
John 1:4-5 connects light with life and people, a theme central in John 9 where Jesus heals the blind man to reveal himself as the light of the world.
Jesus declares himself the light of the world in John 8:12, a claim immediately followed up in chapter 9 with a concrete demonstration of this light through the healing of the blind man.
Similar to John 9, Jesus links suffering to God's glory in John 11:4, where he says that Lazarus' sickness is not unto death but for the glory of God's Son.
